commentary.headline: H1 2025 is a cost-control + survival pack; conversion collapsed; geographic split persists; Q3 guide still negative.

outlook.tone: cautious; stabilise and protect liquidity; no visible inflection yet

interpretation_blunt: Not an inflection pack. Statutory conversion at 0.5% is near-break-even economics; underlying 3.8% is still far below normal.
Geographic split persists: Americas and Asia positive (thesis survival factor), UK/EMEA still the drag and still guided negative into Q3.
Liquidity is thin: net cash ~£10.8m with facilities drawn (RCF + debtor discounting). That’s manageable but reduces margin for error if Q3 worsens.

why: REC June 2025 deteriorated (~38) -> negative signal for UK hiring backdrop.
France business climate still flatlined below 100.
Germany expectations improving but not at an 'open' threshold yet (scale differs; trend positive).

checks: Conversion collapse + low net cash + facilities drawn -> risk rising
watchouts: If Q3 comes in at the low end of guidance AND cash tightens further, Gate 2 could degrade materially.
Any further step-up in restructuring / cost actions that damage capacity can delay recovery.

gate_3_price.note: Price gate is handled by market price feed; this pack alone is not an entry catalyst.

gate_view.overall: NO_TRADE (watch, don’t trade) unless thesis status says ENTER.

next_steps: Ingest the next pack (Q3 / Q3 trading update) and update the same core macro feeds (REC / France / Germany) for Jul–Sep 2025 where applicable.
Confirm whether management commentary indicates France/Germany client behaviour changing (this is the real gating variable for the thesis).
Keep one commentary JSON per period so the dashboard shows a clean timeline across ~10 packs.

commentary.headline: Q3 2025: Europe still weak, but decline narrowed; US and Asia continue to grow; cash improved sharply

guidance.cost_actions: Cost reduction programme on track to deliver annualised savings of c. £15m from 2026; c. £5m H2 2025 savings offsetting part of c. £15m one-off cost

takeaways: This is better than H1 on trend, but still not a clean recovery pack. Group gross profit decline narrowed to -6.7% constant currency from -9.7% in H1.
Europe remains the core drag. France was down 16%, Germany down 11%, and UK down 14.3%.
The US delivered a fourth consecutive quarter of growth (+10%) and Asia delivered a second consecutive quarter of growth (+1%), which is the main offset.
Productivity improved: gross profit per fee earner was up 1% versus Q3 2024, despite continued weak sentiment.
Headcount was cut again by 120, mainly in Europe, which supports productivity but also signals continued caution.
Net cash improved materially to about £38m from about £11m at Q2, which reduces immediate balance-sheet pressure.
FY 2025 operating profit guidance was maintained around £21.5m, which supports stability but still does not confirm a broad cyclical upturn.
notes_for_aion: This is a new period key: 2025-Q3. It should appear in the dropdown once company_trigger_maps/company_PAGE.L/2025-Q3.json exists.
Do not fabricate REC, INSEE, or IFO values; they remain external manual macro inputs.
Trend improved versus H1, but Europe remains weak, so thesis should remain watch unless other trigger evidence improves.
Cash improvement matters positively, but it is not enough by itself to mark a cyclical recovery.

commentary.headline: Q4 2025: US and Asia kept growing, Europe and UK stayed weak; decline narrowed again but recovery still uneven

guidance.cost_actions: Cost programme reduced 2025 costs by c.£5m and remains on track to deliver annualised savings of c.£15m from 2026

takeaways: Trend improved again versus H1 and Q3: Q4 gross profit decline narrowed to -4.6% constant currency.
US and Asia remained the bright spots. The US delivered a fifth straight quarter of growth and Asia a third straight quarter of growth.
Greater China returned to growth for the first time since 2022, which is a notable positive change inside Asia.
Europe and the UK still remain the core problem. France was down 17%, the UK down 10.1%, and Netherlands down 21%.
Germany improved versus Q3 but was still negative at -5%, so it is less bad rather than good.
Productivity improved again, with gross profit per fee earner up 3%, but this was helped by continued headcount reduction.
Net cash softened to about £31m at year-end from about £38m at Q3, though it rebounded to about £40m by 9 January.
This still looks like a controlled trough-management pack rather than a clean cyclical recovery confirmation.

variables.why_it_matters: Germany is 12% of group and declined 23% in Q4 2024 — the worst performing major market; IFO employment expectations lead hiring activity by 1-2 quarters
variables.data_source: IFO Institute — Employment Barometer published monthly
variables.sensitivity_coefficient: Germany 12% of group. Recovery from -23% in Q4 2024 to flat represents approximately 2.8pp improvement in group gross profit growth rate at current revenue weights.
variables.threshold_early: IFO employment expectations >= 97 for 2 consecutive months
variables.threshold_confirm: IFO employment expectations >= 100 for 2 consecutive months
variables.threshold_break: IFO employment expectations <= 93 for 2 consecutive months
variables.thesis_action_on_confirm: Germany stabilising — reduce EMEA headwind estimate
variables.thesis_action_on_break: Germany worsening — EMEA drag intensifying, reduce group estimate
variables.notes: Germany industrial recession is the primary driver of weak recruitment market. Recovery requires either domestic stimulus or export market improvement.

variables.name: EUR/GBP Quarterly Average Rate
variables.why_it_matters: EMEA is 55% of group revenue reported primarily in EUR; EUR/GBP movement directly impacts reported GBP gross profit; Q4 2024 FX was -4.2pp drag on reported growth
variables.data_source: ECB Euro foreign exchange reference rates — daily publication
variables.sensitivity_coefficient: 1% EUR appreciation vs GBP = approximately +0.55% improvement in reported group gross profit (EMEA 55% weight).
variables.threshold_early: quarterly avg EUR/GBP >= 0.845 for 4 consecutive weeks
variables.threshold_confirm: quarterly avg EUR/GBP >= 0.860 for 8 consecutive weeks
variables.threshold_break: quarterly avg EUR/GBP <= 0.820 for 4 consecutive weeks
variables.thesis_action_on_confirm: EUR strength adding to reported gross profit — upgrade reported numbers estimate
variables.thesis_action_on_break: EUR weakness creating FX headwind on reported numbers — reduce reported estimate
variables.notes: EUR/GBP is secondary to market activity as a driver but can swing reported numbers by 3-5pp in volatile FX periods as demonstrated in Q4 2024.

variables.name: Group Fee Earner Headcount
variables.why_it_matters: Fee earner headcount is management's primary operating lever and a direct signal of their confidence in near-term recovery; stabilisation precedes revenue inflection by 1-2 quarters
variables.data_source: PageGroup quarterly trading updates — company RNS filing
variables.sensitivity_coefficient: 100 fee earners at average £157k productivity = approximately £15.7m annual gross profit capacity. Headcount additions take 6-12 months to reach full productivity.
variables.threshold_early: headcount stable — quarterly change between -50 and +50 for 1 quarter
variables.threshold_confirm: headcount growing — quarterly increase >= 100 for 2 consecutive quarters
variables.threshold_break: headcount cut >= 300 in a single quarter
variables.thesis_action_on_confirm: management confidence signal — headcount growth implies pipeline visibility, upgrade forward estimate
variables.thesis_action_on_break: accelerating headcount cuts signal management loss of confidence in near-term recovery — thesis under review
variables.notes: Current level 5,370 at end Q4 2024. Peak was approximately 8,000+ in 2022 boom. Current level reflects deep cycle trough. Stabilisation here is the first positive signal.

variables.name: Group Gross Profit Growth (Constant Currency)
variables.why_it_matters: Primary top-line metric for PageGroup — constant currency growth strips out FX to show underlying business momentum; currently -13.0% in Q4 2024
variables.data_source: PageGroup quarterly trading updates — company RNS filing
variables.sensitivity_coefficient: Improvement from -13% to 0% represents the trough-to-recovery move. Each 5pp improvement in growth rate at current gross profit levels represents approximately £42m of incremental annual gross profit.
variables.threshold_early: gross profit growth >= -5.0% constant currency for 1 quarter
variables.threshold_confirm: gross profit growth >= 0.0% constant currency for 1 quarter
variables.threshold_break: gross profit growth <= -20.0% constant currency for 1 quarter
variables.thesis_action_on_confirm: recovery confirmed — thesis moves to building, consider deployment
variables.thesis_action_on_break: deterioration accelerating — thesis breaks, stand down
variables.notes: Q4 2024 at -13.0% constant currency. FY2024 at -12.9%. Prior cycle trough was approximately -30% in 2009. Current cycle appears less severe.

variables.name: France Gross Profit Growth (Constant Currency)
variables.why_it_matters: France is 15% of group and the highest-leverage market — France recovery disproportionately lifts group operating profit due to high fixed cost base in French operations
variables.data_source: PageGroup quarterly trading updates — company RNS filing
variables.sensitivity_coefficient: France 15% of group. Recovery from -17% to 0% adds approximately £13.5m to group gross profit annually at current run rates. Operating leverage means profit impact is approximately 2x revenue impact.
variables.threshold_early: France gross profit growth >= -10.0% constant currency for 1 quarter
variables.threshold_confirm: France gross profit growth >= -5.0% constant currency for 2 consecutive quarters
variables.threshold_break: France gross profit growth <= -25.0% constant currency for 1 quarter
variables.thesis_action_on_confirm: France recovery underway — most powerful positive signal for group — elevate thesis conviction significantly
variables.thesis_action_on_break: France structural deterioration — review whether cyclical thesis remains valid
variables.notes: France -17% in Q4 2024. This is the market to watch above all others. INSEE confidence is the leading indicator for this variable.

variables.name: Gross Profit Per Fee Earner (Productivity)
variables.why_it_matters: Productivity is the primary operating leverage metric — when GP per fee earner turns positive the fixed cost base creates rapid margin expansion; currently -5% vs prior year
variables.data_source: PageGroup quarterly trading updates — derived: gross profit divided by fee earner headcount
variables.sensitivity_coefficient: 1% productivity improvement on 5,370 fee earners at £157k average = approximately £8.4m incremental gross profit at near-100% incremental margin.
variables.threshold_early: productivity change >= -2.0% vs prior year for 1 quarter
variables.threshold_confirm: productivity change >= 0.0% vs prior year for 2 consecutive quarters
variables.threshold_break: productivity change <= -15.0% vs prior year for 1 quarter
variables.thesis_action_on_confirm: productivity inflection — operating leverage turning positive, margin recovery imminent
variables.thesis_action_on_break: productivity deteriorating severely — cost base not covered, thesis breaks
variables.notes: Calculated from trading update data: Q4 2024 gross profit £196.7m / 5,370 fee earners = £36.6k per quarter = £146k annualised. Down 5% vs Q4 2023.
